TempleCBE: Biostatistics, Clinical Data Science, and Modeling Utilities

Source: R/TempleCBE-package.R
TempleCBE-package.Rd

Utilities of Temple University's Center for Biostatistics and Epidemiology (CBE): statistical tests and report tables, data-quality and missingness displays, recipe steps for tidymodels, penalized Cox models with nested cross-validation and survival metrics, checkpointed long-running computations, and report rendering and delivery.

Naming

Functions that begin with `cbe_` are presentation and formatting functions in the Temple CBE style (themes, palettes, scales, plots, report tables, number formatters). Every other function is named for what it does, for example [nested_survival_run()], [cox_single()], [checkpoint_map()] and [describe_columns()]. Some S3 classes keep a `cbe_` prefix from earlier versions; these are class names, not functions, and are kept so that saved objects and `inherits()` checks continue to work.

Where to start

* Survival modeling: [coxnet()], [cv_coxnet()], [nested_cv_coxnet()], [nested_survival_run()]. * Long computations that resume after an interruption: [checkpoint_map()]. * Reports: [theme_cbe()], [cbe_cox_table()], [bundle_deliverables()]. * Calls to functions renamed in earlier versions: [find_deprecated_calls()].

The vignettes (`browseVignettes("TempleCBE")`) and the website <https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/> have worked examples.
